raw_response:
Well, it's almost October now, time to get the winter wheat in the ground. I've been farming these 6 mu for 15 years, ever since my father handed me the land when I turned 30. With 7 mouths to feed at home — my parents, my wife, our two kids, and my younger brother who helps out — I can't afford to take risks. Every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back, preferably with something extra.

**My land and my system**

All 6 mu go into the wheat-maize double crop. That's been our system for generations here in Quzhou. The wheat goes in around October 8th to 12th, depending on when the rains soften the soil. Last year I planted on the 10th and it worked out fine. The maize gets seeded right after wheat harvest in early June — sometimes I barely have 5 days between taking the wheat off and getting the maize in. That's just how it is. No time for deep plowing in June; I rely on rotary tillage right after harvest.

**Wheat decisions**

For seed, I'll buy the improved wheat variety from the supply shop in town — probably Jimai 22 or something similar the dealer recommends. Costs about 40 yuan per mu. I don't save my own seed; the yield drops too much, and with only 6 mu I can't afford that gamble.

Fertilizer is where I really have to think. The extension technician at the village meeting last spring said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've always done a bit more because my soil is decent but not great. Here's what I'll do: before sowing, I'll broadcast about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, one bag covers about one mu. Then at jointing, around Qingming festival in early April, if the wheat looks a little yellow I'll topdress another 25 kg of urea per mu. That's what my neighbor Lao Zhang does, and he gets good yields. I can't afford to buy much more than that. The compound gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, which is important because I never apply those separately.

I'll irrigate three times: once in late November or early December before the ground freezes — this "winter water" is crucial; once at jointing in March or April; and once at grain filling in May. Each time costs about 50 yuan per mu for electricity to pump from the well. Three times is what most people around here do, and my well has enough water.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once after sowing to control weeds — about 15 yuan per mu. If I see aphids in spring, I'll spray insecticide too. Fungicide? I usually skip it unless the weather is really wet and disease shows up. That's another 20 yuan or so if needed.

Tillage before wheat: I'll hire the rotary tiller from the village cooperative. Costs about 50 yuan per mu. I don't own one myself — too expensive for 6 mu.

Harvest in early June: I'll hire the combine harvester. They charge about 50 yuan per mu now. My brother and I can handle getting the grain home.

For labor: sowing, fertilizing, and irrigating are mostly me, my brother, and my wife. I figure about 12 family days for the whole wheat season, plus maybe 2 hired days at harvest if we're short on time.

Yield expectation? Last year I got about 480 kg per mu. The soil looks similar this year, so I'm hoping for around 480–500 kg per mu. If I get 500, that's a good year.

**Maize decisions**

After wheat harvest in early June, I have to move fast. I'll hire the rotary tiller to go over the field once — shallow, just to break up the stubble. Then plant the hybrid maize seed right away. Hybrid seed costs about 55 yuan per mu. I always buy fresh hybrid seed; saved seed doesn't perform.

For fertilizer, I put it all down at planting — there's no time for topdressing later, and anyway I'm usually too busy with other work. I'll use about 45 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, the same 15-15-15 type. That's less than what I use for wheat because maize grows fast and the season is shorter. Some years I wish I'd put more, but the money isn't there.

Irrigation for maize: I'll water at planting if it's dry, and then once more at the filling stage in August. Sometimes twice if it's a really dry summer. Let's say 2 times this year, about 50 yuan per mu each time.

Herbicide once after emergence — about 12 yuan per mu. Insecticide if I see corn borer, which I usually do, so I'll spray once. That's another 15 yuan or so.

For labor: planting and fertilizing are family work — me, my brother, and sometimes my father if he's feeling up to it. About 8 family days. Harvest in late September is mostly hired because we need to get it done fast before the autumn rains; hire a combine for about 80 yuan per mu. I'll need maybe 3 hired days for harvest and transport.

Yield expectation: last year I got about 520 kg per mu on the maize. I'll aim for about 500–520 kg per mu this year.

**What I'm worried about**

Money is always tight. With 7 people, we need to keep some grain for our own consumption — at least 1000 kg of wheat for the year. The rest I sell. Maize mostly goes to the buyer who drives through the village. I need to make sure I have cash left over after inputs for emergencies. My younger daughter starts middle school next year and the fees will go up.

The tradeoff is always fertilizer versus cash in hand. I know I could probably get more yield with more fertilizer, but I can't risk running out of money if someone gets sick. So I stick to what I know works — a bit more than the extension guy says, but not so much that I'm stretched thin.
